subsection.name: SC-1
description: Develop, document, and disseminate to organization defined personnel or roles
Organization level, mission/business process level, system level system and communication protection policy that
Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance
Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines
Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the system and communications protection policy and the associated system and communications protection controls
Designate an organization defined official to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the system and communications protection policy and procedures
Review and update current system and communications protection policy and procedures

subsection.name: SC-2
description: Separate user functionality, including user interface services, from system management functionality

subsection.name: SC-3
description: Isolate security functions from nonsecurity functions

subsection.name: SC-4
description: Prevent unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources

subsection.name: SC-5
description: Protect against, limit the effects of the following types of denial of service events
Employ organization defined controls to achieve the denial of service objective

subsection.name: SC-6
description: Protect the availability of resource by allocating organization defined resources by priority, quota, organization defined controls

subsection.name: SC-7
description: Monitor and control communications at the external managed interfaces to the system and at key internal managed interfaces within the system
Implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are physically, logically separated from internal organization networks
Connect to external networks or systems only through managed interfaces consisting of boundary protection devices arranged in accordance with an organizational security and privacy architecture

subsection.name: SC-8
description: Protect confidentiality, integrity of transmitted information

subsection.name: SC-10
description: Terminate the network connection associated with a communication session at the end of the session or after organization defined time period of inactivity

subsection.name: SC-11
description: Provide a physically, logically isolated trusted communications path for communications between the user and the trusted components of the system

Permit users to invoke the trusted communications path for communications between the user and the following security functions of the system, including at a minimum, authentication and re-authentication

subsection.name: SC-12
description: Establish and manage cryptographic keys when cryptography is employed within the system in accordance with the following key management requirements

subsection.name: SC-13
description: Determines the organization defined cryptographic uses
Implement organization defined types of cryptography for each specified cryptographic use

subsection.name: SC-15
description: Prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices and applications with the following exceptions
Provide an explicit indication of use to users physically present at the devices

subsection.name: SC-16
description: Associate organization defined security and privacy attributes with information exchanged between systems and between system components

subsection.name: SC-17
description: Issue public key certificates under an organization defined certificate policy or obtain public key certificates from an approved service provider
Include only approved trust anchors in trust stores or certificate stores managed by the organization

subsection.name: SC-18
description: Define acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies
Authorize, monitor, and control the use of mobile code within the system

subsection.name: SC-20
description: Provide additional data origin authentication and integrity verification artifacts along with the authoritative name resolution data the system returns in response to external name/address resolution queries

Provide the means to indicate the security status of child zones and (if the child supports secure resolution services) to enable verification of a chain of trust among parent and child domains, when operating as part of a distributed, hierarchical namespace

subsection.name: SC-21
description: Request and perform data origin authentication and data integrity verification on the name/address resolution responses the system receives from authoritative sources

subsection.name: SC-22
description: Ensure the systems that collectively provide name/address resolution service for an organization are fault-tolerant and implement internal and external role separation

subsection.name: SC-23
description: Protect the authenticity of communications sessions

subsection.name: SC-24
description: Fail to an organization defined known system state for the following failures on the indicated components while preserving organization defined system state information in failure

subsection.name: SC-25
description: Employ minimal functionality and information storage on the following system components

subsection.name: SC-26
description: Include components within organizational systems specifically designed to be the target of malicious attacks for detecting, deflecting, and analyzing such attacks

subsection.name: SC-27
description: Include within organizational systems the following platform independent applications

subsection.name: SC-28
description: Protect the confidentiality, integrity of the following information at rest

subsection.name: SC-29
description: Employ a diverse set of information technologies for the following system components in the implementation of the system

subsection.name: SC-30
description: Employ the following concealment and misdirection techniques for organization defined systems at organization defined time periods to confuse and mislead adversaries

subsection.name: SC-31
description: Perform a covert channel analysis to identify those aspects of communications within the system that are potential avenues for covert storage, timing channels
Estimate the maximum bandwidth of those channels

subsection.name: SC-32
description: Partition the system into organization defined system components residing in separate physical, logical domains or environments based on organization fiend circumstances for physical or logical separation of components

subsection.name: SC-34
description: For organization defined system components, load and execute
The operating environment from hardware-enforced, read-only media
Organization defined applications from hardware enforced, read only media

subsection.name: SC-35
description: Include system components that proactively seek to identify network-based malicious code or malicious websites

subsection.name: SC-36
description: Distribute the following processing and storage components across multiple physical location, logical domains

subsection.name: SC-37
description: Employ the following out of band channels for the physical delivery or electronic transmission of organization defined information, system components, or devices to organization defined individuals or systems

subsection.name: SC-38
description: Employ the following operations security controls to protect key organizational information throughout the system development life cycle

subsection.name: SC-39
description: Maintain a separate execution domain for each executing system process

subsection.name: SC-40
description: Protect external and internal organization defined wireless links from the following signal parameter attacks

subsection.name: SC-41
description: Physically, logically disable or remove organization defined connection ports or input/output devices on the following systems or system components

subsection.name: SC-42
description: Prohibit the use of devices possessing organization defined environmental sensing capabilities in organization defined facilities, areas, or systems, the remotes activation of environmental sensing capabilities on organizational systems or system components with the following exceptions
Provide an explicit indication of sensor use to organization defined group of users

subsection.name: SC-43
description: Establish usage restrictions and implementation guidelines for the following system components
Authorize, monitor, and control the use of such components within the system

subsection.name: SC-44
description: Employ a detonation chamber capability within organization defined system, system component, or location

subsection.name: SC-45
description: Synchronize system clocks within and between systems and system components

subsection.name: SC-46
description: Implement a policy enforcement mechanism physically, logically between the physical and/or network interfaces for the connecting security domains

subsection.name: SC-47
description: Establish organization defined alternate communication paths for system operations organizational command and control

subsection.name: SC-48
description: Relocate organization defined sensors and monitoring capabilities to organization defined locations under the following conditions or circumstances

subsection.name: SC-49
description: Implement hardware-enforced separation and policy enforcement mechanisms between organization defined security domains

subsection.name: SC-50
description: Implement software enforced separation and policy enforcement mechanisms between organization defined security domains

subsection.name: SC-51
description: Employ hardware based, write protect for organization defined system firmware components

Implement specific procedures for organization defined authorized individuals to manually disable hardware write protect for firmware modifications and enable the write product prior to returning to operational mode
